about: Batch 04, slice A, chunk A29: lunches (sandwiches, wraps, tacos, tarts, noodle and rice bowls) from France, the US, the UK, Mexico, the Middle East, Japan, Korea, China, Thailand and Indonesia.

recipes.title: Jambon-Beurre (French Ham and Butter Baguette)
recipes.summary: The Parisian lunch classic: crisp baguette, soft butter, good ham and a swipe of Dijon.
steps: Split the baguette lengthways, leaving one edge attached, and cut it in half crossways.
Spread both cut sides generously with the butter and the mustard.
Layer the ham and the sliced pickles along the base, close firmly and press down until the filling holds together.
Eat straight away, or wrap tightly for the lunchbox.
notes: Food safety: ham is ready to eat but should stay below 5°C. For a packed lunch keep it in an insulated bag with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours, or refrigerate until lunch.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Pan Bagnat (Nicoise Tuna Sandwich)
recipes.summary: Tuna, egg, anchovy, tomato and olives pressed into a roll with olive oil, made for the beach.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool under cold water, peel and slice.
Split the rolls and pull out a little crumb from the middle. Mix the oil and vinegar and brush it over the cut sides.
Layer the tuna, tomato, cucumber, onion, olives, anchovy, egg and basil in the rolls, then close and press firmly.
Wrap tightly and press under a weight for 15 minutes, until the bread has soaked up the juices.
notes: Food safety: hard-boiled egg and tuna must stay below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an insulated bag with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, fish and gluten.

recipes.title: Muffuletta (New Orleans Olive Salad Sandwich)
recipes.summary: A big sandwich of salami, ham and mozzarella with a punchy chopped olive and artichoke salad that soaks into the bread.
steps: Stir the olives, artichoke, roasted capsicum, oil, vinegar, garlic and oregano together in a bowl.
Slice the loaf in half horizontally and pull out a little of the soft middle. Spread the olive salad over both cut sides.
Layer the ham, salami and mozzarella on the base, close, wrap tightly and press under a weight for 20 minutes, until the bread is soaked through, then cut into four wedges.
notes: Food safety: cured meats and cheese should stay below 5°C. Wrapped wedges keep in the fridge for 2 days; for a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Cubano (Cuban Pressed Pork and Ham Sandwich)
recipes.summary: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and mustard in buttered bread, pressed in a pan until crisp and melted.
steps: Split the bread lengths, butter the outsides and spread the mustard inside.
Layer the pork, ham, cheese and pickles, and close.
Cook in a hot frying pan over medium heat, pressing down firmly with a heavy pan or a plate, for 4 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Slice on the diagonal and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: use cooked roast pork that has been chilled promptly. The sandwich should be steaming hot in the middle after pressing; eat within 4 hours if packed, with an ice pack until you can reheat it.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Chicken Shawarma Wrap (with Garlic Yoghurt)
recipes.summary: Spiced chicken thigh seared hard and rolled in flatbread with garlic yoghurt, tomato and pickled turnip.
steps: Toss the chicken with the spices, 2 of the garlic cloves, the oil, half the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt.
Sear in a very hot pan in two batches for 5 minutes each, until browned and cooked through to 75°C.
Mix the yoghurt with the remaining garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the flatbreads, spread with the yoghurt and fill with chicken, tomato, cucumber and turnip. Roll tightly.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest piece with no pink. Cool leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch keep with an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Egg Salad Sandwich (with Chives)
recipes.summary: Creamy chopped egg with mustard and chives on soft white bread with crisp lettuce, a lunchbox staple.
steps: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to the boil and cook for 10 minutes. Cool in cold water, then peel.
Chop the eggs roughly and mix until creamy but still chunky, with the mayonnaise, mustard, chives, a pinch of salt and pepper.
Pile onto two slices of bread with the lettuce and top with the remaining bread. Cut in half.
notes: Food safety: egg mixtures spoil quickly. Keep below 5°C, pack with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours, or keep in the fridge until lunch.
Contains egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Bacon Butty (English Bacon Roll)
recipes.summary: Crisp streaky bacon in a buttered soft roll with a squirt of tomato sauce, the 10-minute brunch-or-lunch fix.
steps: Cook the bacon in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, turning once, until crisp and well browned with no pink.
Split and butter the rolls.
Fill with the bacon and the sauce and eat hot.
notes: Food safety: bacon must be cooked right through until the fat is rendered and the meat is no longer pink. Eat hot; if packed, keep chilled and reheat until steaming.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Chip Butty (English Hot Chips in Buttered Bread)
recipes.summary: Oven chips in soft buttered white bread with malt vinegar, the comfort lunch of northern England.
steps: Bake the chips on a tray at 220°C (200°C fan) for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Butter the bread and pile the hot chips onto two slices. Sprinkle with the vinegar and salt, add the sauce and top with the remaining bread.
Press down gently and eat while hot.
notes: Eat straight away, as the chips go soft in the bread.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Torta de Jamon (Mexican Ham Roll with Avocado)
recipes.summary: A toasted roll of ham, melted cheese, avocado and pickled jalapeno, a Mexico City street lunch.
steps: Split the rolls and toast the cut sides in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Spread with mayonnaise and layer the ham and cheese on the base. Grill for 2 minutes, until the cheese melts.
Top with the avocado, jalapeno, tomato and lettuce, close and press down.
notes: Food safety: ham should stay below 5°C until cooking. Eat hot; if packed, keep chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Tacos de Papa (Mexican Crispy Potato Tacos)
recipes.summary: Spiced mashed potato folded into corn tortillas and crisped in a pan, topped with lettuce, salsa and a little cheese.
steps: Boil the potato in salted water for 15 minutes, until soft. Drain and mash roughly.
Cook the onion in the first oil for 4 minutes, stir in the spices, then mix into the potato and season.
Warm the tortillas to soften them. Put 2 tbsp of potato on one half of each, fold over and press the edges.
Fry the tacos in the second oil for 2 minutes each side, until crisp and golden.
Top with lettuce, salsa, sour cream and crumbled feta.
notes: Eat hot for the best crunch. The potato filling keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Contains milk.

recipes.title: Tarte a la Moutarde (French Tomato and Mustard Tart)
recipes.summary: A Burgundy-style tart of puff pastry brushed with sharp Dijon, layered with ripe tomato and melted mozzarella.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Lay the pastry on a lined tray and score a border 2cm in.
Spread the mustard inside the border, then layer the cheese and tomatoes.
Scatter the thyme, drizzle with oil and season with pepper.
Bake for 28 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and golden.
notes: Eat warm or at room temperature. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Tamago Sando (Japanese Egg Sandwich)
recipes.summary: Ultra-soft egg salad with Japanese mayonnaise in fluffy white bread, crusts trimmed.
steps: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Mash the eggs with the mayonnaise, milk, sugar and a pinch of salt until creamy but still a little chunky.
Butter the bread, spread the filling thickly on two slices and top with the rest. Trim off the crusts and cut in half.
notes: Food safety: keep the filling below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Chicken Bento (with Egg and Edamame)
recipes.summary: Glazed chicken thigh, rolled omelette, edamame and carrot packed over rice in a box that eats well cold.
steps: Sear the chicken in the first oil for 6 minutes, add the teriyaki sauce and cook for 3 more minutes, until glossy and cooked through to 75°C.
Whisk the eggs with the soy sauce and sugar. Cook in the second oil in a small pan over low heat, rolling it up as it sets, about 5 minutes, then slice.
Boil the edamame and carrot for 3 minutes and drain.
Pack the rice into two boxes and arrange the chicken, egg, edamame and carrot on top. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Cool the rice and chicken quickly, then keep below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, soy and sesame.

recipes.title: Oyakodon (Japanese Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
recipes.summary: Tender chicken and onion simmered in a sweet soy broth, finished with loosely set egg over steaming rice.
steps: Simmer the stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a wide pan. Add the onion and chicken and cook for 8 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Pour the egg over in a circle, cover and cook for 2 minutes, until just set but still soft.
Slide it over the rice in two bowls and top with spring onion.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and the egg should be set, not runny. Best eaten straight away; refrigerate leftovers within an hour and eat within a day.
Contains egg, soy and gluten.

recipes.title: Chicken Yakisoba (Japanese Stir-Fried Noodles)
recipes.summary: Chewy wheat noodles tossed with chicken, cabbage and carrot in a tangy Worcestershire and soy sauce.
steps: Loosen the noodles in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Stir-fry the chicken in half the oil over high heat for 5 minutes, until cooked through to 75°C. Remove.
Stir-fry the cabbage and carrot in the remaining oil for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles, chicken, sauces and sugar and toss for 2 minutes. Scatter with spring onion.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, soy and fish (Worcestershire sauce).

recipes.title: Korean Egg Toast (Gilgeori Toast)
recipes.summary: A thick vegetable omelette in buttery toast with a sprinkle of sugar, the Seoul street breakfast.
steps: Beat the eggs with the cabbage, carrot, spring onion and a pinch of salt.
Melt a little butter in a pan and toast the bread on both sides for about 2 minutes each, until golden. Set aside.
Pour half the egg mixture into the pan, shape into a square the size of the bread and cook for 3 minutes, folding the edges in and flipping once, until fully set. Repeat.
Sprinkle the toast with sugar, put the omelette on, squeeze on the tomato sauce and close, pressing until the toast is warm through.
notes: Food safety: the egg must be cooked through with no wet patches. Eat straight away.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Pad See Ew (Thai Soy Sauce Rice Noodles with Chicken)
recipes.summary: Wide, charred rice noodles with chicken, egg and gai lan in a sweet-savoury dark soy sauce, a 20-minute wok lunch.
steps: Separate the noodles gently, microwaving for 30 seconds if they are stiff.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil in a hot wok for 4 minutes, until cooked through to 75°C. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Push to one side, scramble the eggs in the gap, then add the gai lan stems for 1 minute.
Add the noodles, sauces and sugar and toss for 3 minutes, until some noodles catch and char, adding the leaves for the last minute.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Cool and refrigerate leftovers within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, soy and gluten.

recipes.title: Egg Fried Rice (with Peas and Spring Onion)
recipes.summary: Day-old rice fried hot with scrambled egg, peas and carrot, a 10-minute lunch for leftover rice.
steps: Beat the eggs. Heat half the oil in a wok and scramble the eggs for 1 minute, then remove.
Fry the carrot in the remaining oil for 2 minutes, add the peas and the cold rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Return the egg, add the soy sauce, sesame oil and spring onion and toss until the rice is steaming hot.
notes: Food safety: use rice that was cooled within an hour of cooking and kept below 5°C for no more than a day. Never reheat rice twice. Eat hot; for a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, soy and sesame.

recipes.title: Mie Goreng (Indonesian Sweet Soy Prawn Noodles)
recipes.summary: Egg noodles wok-tossed with prawns, egg and cabbage in sweet kecap manis with a kick of sambal.
steps: Cook the noodles per the packet until tender, drain and toss with a little oil.
Stir-fry the shallot and garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the prawns for 2 minutes until pink and opaque, then push aside.
Scramble the eggs in the gap, then add the cabbage for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, kecap manis, soy sauce and sambal and toss for 3 minutes. Top with fried shallots.
notes: Food safety: prawns must be pink and opaque throughout. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and eat within a day; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains crustacean, egg, gluten and soy.

recipes.title: Singapore Noodles (Curried Vermicelli with Prawn and Egg)
recipes.summary: Thin rice vermicelli stir-fried with curry powder, prawns, egg, capsicum and bean sprouts, light and fragrant.
steps: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain and snip into shorter lengths.
Scramble the eggs in half the oil for 1 minute and remove.
Stir-fry the prawns for 2 minutes until pink and opaque, add the capsicum and curry powder for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, sesame oil, egg, sprouts and spring onion and toss for 2 minutes.
notes: Food safety: prawns must be pink and opaque right through. Cool and refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains crustacean, egg and soy.
